questions.question: Explain the difference between direct and indirect distance, and give two reasons why indirect distances are longer.
questions.expected_answer: Direct distance is the straight-line distance between two places; indirect distance is measured along an actual route such as a road, railway or river. Indirect distances are longer because routes bend around obstacles such as mountains, rivers, buildings and property, climb passes in zigzags, and rivers meander.

questions.question: Describe the five steps of the string method for measuring a curving road using a line scale.
questions.expected_answer: Use thin, non-stretchy string; fix one end on the start point; lay the string carefully along every bend of the route; pinch or mark the string at the end point; straighten it and lay it along the line scale from zero, adding full bar lengths if needed, to read the distance.

questions.question: A route has three straight sections measuring 3.2 cm, 4.5 cm and 1.3 cm on a map with the scale 1 cm represents 100 m. The direct distance measures 6.5 cm. Calculate the route length and the extra distance.
